rules.quote: C→Rust translations must convert `RtlZeroMemory`/`memset` byte counts to element counts for `write_bytes`
rules.rule: When translating C code to Rust, convert `RtlZeroMemory`/`memset` byte counts to element counts before passing them to `core::ptr::write_bytes`.

rules.quote: Use `ninja boot/bootdata/system` for the ramdisk hive.
rules.rule: To build the SYSTEM hive used by the ramdisk, run `ninja boot/bootdata/system`, not `ninja bootcd_hives`.

rules.quote: CGU=1 must be a coordinated change:
rules.rule: Treat setting codegen-units = 1 as a coordinated change, not a drop-in toggle, when applying it to this project.

rules.quote: Set `codegen-units = 1`
rules.rule: Set codegen-units = 1 in Cargo.toml as part of the coordinated CGU=1 change.

rules.quote: Revert ObCreateObjectAddress_shim → back to ObCreateObject_shim returning PVOID
rules.rule: When applying the CGU=1 change, revert ObCreateObjectAddress_shim back to ObCreateObject_shim returning PVOID.

rules.quote: Revert IopFinishCreatedDeviceObject → merge back into IoCreateDevice
rules.rule: When applying the CGU=1 change, merge IopFinishCreatedDeviceObject back into IoCreateDevice.

rules.quote: Revert IopFinishIoInitSystem → merge back into IoInitSystem
rules.rule: When applying the CGU=1 change, merge IopFinishIoInitSystem back into IoInitSystem.

rules.quote: Revert RTL string shims → use direct imports
rules.rule: When applying the CGU=1 change, revert the RTL string shims and use direct imports instead.

rules.quote: Remove the ARM64 `#[inline(never)]` on PspCreateThread
rules.rule: When applying the CGU=1 change, remove the ARM64 #[inline(never)] attribute on PspCreateThread.

rules.quote: Test all 3 arches
rules.rule: After applying the CGU=1 change, test on all 3 architectures.

rules.quote: Run `codex exec --full-auto "prompt"` for non-interactive translation
rules.rule: When running the Codex CLI for C-to-Rust translation, invoke it non-interactively with `codex exec --full-auto "prompt"`.

rules.quote: Default model works (o3 requires paid API, not ChatGPT account)
rules.rule: When using the Codex CLI, use the default model rather than o3, since o3 requires a paid API account.

rules.quote: Provide detailed translation rules in the prompt (pool tag encoding, NT_ERROR vs NT_SUCCESS, extern "system", DUMMY_PSEH SEH handling, addr_of_mut! for events, etc.)
rules.rule: When prompting the Codex CLI for C-to-Rust translation, include detailed translation rules in the prompt covering pool tag encoding, NT_ERROR vs NT_SUCCESS, extern "system", DUMMY_PSEH SEH handling, and addr_of_mut! for events.

rules.quote: Always run `verify_constants.py` on the output to catch wrong constant values
rules.rule: After Codex CLI produces translation output, always run verify_constants.py on it to catch wrong constant values.

rules.quote: Always add missing extern declarations, constants, and type casts manually after integration
rules.rule: After integrating Codex CLI translation output, always manually add any missing extern declarations, constants, and type casts.

rules.quote: The CLI reads files from the repo, so point it at both the C source and existing Rust patterns
rules.rule: When prompting the Codex CLI for translation, point it at both the C source files and existing Rust patterns in the repo.

rules.quote: Don't make commits just for retranslations or intermediate progress.
rules.rule: Do not make a git commit just for retranslations or other intermediate progress.

rules.quote: Only commit when smoke tests pass or there's a meaningful working state change.
rules.rule: Only make a commit when smoke tests pass or when there is a meaningful working state change.

rules.quote: Keep debugging until the file actually works.
rules.rule: Keep debugging a file until it actually works before committing.

rules.quote: When retranslating a file, immediately proceed to activate it, test it, debug any issues, and only commit once it's either working or you've exhausted debugging and need to document why it's blocked.
rules.rule: When retranslating a file, immediately proceed to activate it, test it, and debug any issues.

rules.quote: only commit once it's either working or you've exhausted debugging and need to document why it's blocked.
rules.rule: After retranslating a file, commit only once it is working or once debugging is exhausted and the blocker needs to be documented.

rules.quote: ALL hand-written extern blocks for Windows kernel NTAPI functions MUST use `extern "system"`, not `extern "C"`
rules.rule: When writing hand-written extern blocks for Windows kernel NTAPI functions, declare them with `extern "system"`, not `extern "C"`.

rules.quote: Only true C-runtime functions (sprintf, wcslen, memset, etc.) should be `extern "C"`
rules.rule: Declare only true C-runtime functions (such as sprintf, wcslen, memset) as `extern "C"`.

rules.quote: RTL string functions (RtlInitAnsiString, RtlAnsiStringToUnicodeString, etc.) that are NTAPI should use shims or `extern "system"`
rules.rule: For NTAPI RTL string functions (such as RtlInitAnsiString, RtlAnsiStringToUnicodeString), use a shim or declare them with `extern "system"`, not `extern "C"`.

rules.quote: When enabling Rust modules on i386, audit ALL `extern "C"` blocks first — grep for `extern "C"` and verify each function
rules.rule: When enabling Rust modules on i386, audit all `extern "C"` blocks first by grepping for `extern "C"` and verifying each function's calling convention.

rules.quote: When in doubt, use bindgen-generated imports from `ntkrnl_sys::ddk::` which have correct calling conventions
rules.rule: When unsure about a kernel function's calling convention, use the bindgen-generated imports from `ntkrnl_sys::ddk::`.

rules.quote: NEVER index bindgen flexible arrays directly (e.g., `array[i]`)
rules.rule: Never index a bindgen-generated flexible array member directly (e.g., `array[i]`) in Rust; access its elements via pointer arithmetic instead.

rules.quote: Use pointer arithmetic: `core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*ptr).field[0]).add(i)` to get slot, `*slot` to read
rules.rule: When reading elements of a bindgen flexible array, use pointer arithmetic (e.g., `core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*ptr).field[0]).add(i)` to get the slot, then `*slot` to read) rather than indexing.

rules.quote: Or use `.as_ptr().add(i)` pattern (already used correctly in plugplay.rs)
rules.rule: Alternatively, when accessing a bindgen flexible array element, use the `.as_ptr().add(i)` pattern rather than direct indexing.

rules.quote: When reviewing Rust kernel translations, grep for `Objects[` or similar array indexing on bindgen types and check if the underlying C struct has a flexible array member
rules.rule: When reviewing Rust kernel translations, search for array indexing on bindgen types (e.g., `Objects[`) and verify whether the underlying C struct has a flexible array member.

rules.quote: Don't remove `#[inline(never)]` from shim_exports.rs.
rules.rule: Do not remove the `#[inline(never)]` annotations from functions in shim_exports.rs.

rules.quote: The `#[inline(never)]` and guards/write_volatile are defense-in-depth — both are needed.
rules.rule: Keep both `#[inline(never)]` and the guards/write_volatile defenses in shim_exports.rs; do not treat either as optional when the other is present.

rules.quote: don't waste time with inline asm / read_volatile / black_box — go straight to structural fixes
rules.rule: When fighting LLVM optimization on i386, do not use inline asm, read_volatile, or black_box as workarounds; go straight to structural fixes.

rules.quote: For output-pointer functions: C shim returning ULONG_PTR > C shim returning PVOID > inline asm
rules.rule: For output-pointer functions on i386, prefer a C shim returning ULONG_PTR over a C shim returning PVOID, and prefer a C shim returning PVOID over inline asm.

rules.quote: For large functions with multiple call sites that trigger optimizer: split into `#[inline(never)]` helpers
rules.rule: For large functions with multiple call sites that trigger the optimizer, split them into `#[inline(never)]` helpers.

rules.quote: on i386 you may also need integer-return + provenance reconstruction
rules.rule: On i386, for the captures(none) cross-CGU issue, use integer return plus provenance reconstruction when a C shim alone is not sufficient.

rules.quote: Codex's approach: emit LLVM IR (`--emit=llvm-ir`), search for `unreachable` after the suspect call, trace back to the bad assumption
rules.rule: When diagnosing LLVM optimization problems, emit LLVM IR (`--emit=llvm-ir`), search for `unreachable` after the suspect call, and trace back to the bad assumption.

rules.quote: Do not make git commits without asking the user first.
rules.rule: Do not create git commits without first asking the user for permission.

rules.quote: stage and describe what would be committed, then ask "shall I commit?" before running `git commit`.
rules.rule: After completing work, stage the changes and describe what would be committed, then ask the user "shall I commit?" before running git commit.

rules.quote: Never use `git checkout --`, `git restore`, or delete files to discard uncommitted work.
rules.rule: Never use git checkout --, git restore, or delete files to discard uncommitted work.

rules.quote: Always use `git stash` to preserve changes.
rules.rule: Always use git stash to preserve uncommitted changes before discarding or temporarily reverting them.

rules.quote: Use `git stash save "description"` to preserve ALL uncommitted work first
rules.rule: When bisecting regressions or temporarily reverting changes, use git stash save "description" to preserve all uncommitted work first.

rules.quote: Use `git stash push -m "description" -- file1 file2` to stash specific files
rules.rule: When bisecting regressions or temporarily reverting changes, use git stash push -m "description" -- file1 file2 to stash specific files.

rules.quote: Never use `git checkout -- file` or `git restore file` on work that was expensive to produce (LLM translations, subagent output, etc.)
rules.rule: Never use git checkout -- file or git restore file on work that was expensive to produce, such as LLM translations or subagent output.

rules.quote: After bisecting, use `git stash pop` or `git stash apply` to restore
rules.rule: After bisecting, use git stash pop or git stash apply to restore stashed changes.

rules.quote: Run after any translation to catch ABI bugs before they cause i386 ud2 crashes.
rules.rule: After any translation, run tools/rustconv/rustconv/verify_abi.py to catch ABI bugs before they cause i386 ud2 crashes.

rules.quote: Should be added to the rustconv post-integration checklist alongside verify_constants.py.
rules.rule: Add verify_abi.py to the rustconv post-integration checklist alongside verify_constants.py.

rules.quote: Stdcall can be fixed by changing to `extern "system"`
rules.rule: When verify_abi.py reports a stdcall mismatch, fix it by changing the function's extern block to extern "system".

rules.quote: need C shims since Rust doesn't have stable `extern "fastcall"`
rules.rule: When verify_abi.py reports a fastcall mismatch, handle it with a C shim, because Rust has no stable extern "fastcall".

rules.quote: Don't use `Volatile<T>` for `#[no_mangle] pub static` globals that are written to.
rules.rule: Do not use `Volatile<T>` for `#[no_mangle] pub static` globals that are written to.

rules.quote: Instead use `read_volatile`/`write_volatile` on the raw `static mut` pointer.
rules.rule: For `#[no_mangle] pub static` globals that are written to, use `read_volatile`/`write_volatile` on the raw `static mut` pointer instead of `Volatile<T>`.

rules.quote: `Volatile<T>` is safe for internal (non-exported) statics, or for statics that are only read.
rules.rule: `Volatile<T>` may be used for internal (non-exported) statics, or for statics that are only read.

rules.quote: Could use `static mut X: Volatile<KIRQL>`
rules.rule: For `#[no_mangle] pub static` globals that are written to, you may use `static mut X: Volatile<KIRQL>` as an alternative.

rules.quote: Never read `.png`/`.jpg`/`.bmp` files during long debugging sessions
rules.rule: Never read .png, .jpg, or .bmp image files with the Read tool during long debugging sessions.

rules.quote: Use `file <path>` or `identify <path>` to check image metadata instead of reading the raw file
rules.rule: To check an image's metadata, run `file <path>` or `identify <path>` instead of reading the raw image file.

rules.quote: If you must inspect a screenshot, use a subagent
rules.rule: If you must inspect a screenshot, delegate the inspection to a subagent so the image stays out of the main context.

rules.quote: use `#define ARCNAME_RUST_REASSIGN` + `#ifndef` guards
rules.rule: When arcname.rs (providing IopReassignSystemRoot/IopVerifyDiskSignature) is used alongside arcname.c (providing IopCreateArcNames), guard the overlapping code with `#define ARCNAME_RUST_REASSIGN` and `#ifndef` guards.

rules.quote: Check this before starting IO translation work.
rules.rule: Before starting any IO subsystem translation work, check the IO translation status file.

rules.quote: Update after changes.
rules.rule: After making changes to IO subsystem translation work, update the IO translation status file.

rules.quote: must be inlined in Rust, not extern
rules.rule: When translating code to Rust, inline the C macro InitializeObjectAttributes rather than declaring it as an extern function.

rules.quote: need explicit null terminators in Rust byte arrays
rules.rule: When sprintf/printf format strings are used in Rust byte arrays, include an explicit null terminator in each format string.

rules.quote: use C shims
rules.rule: When LLVM cross-CGU captures(none) eliminates output pointer writes, use C shims instead of relying on the Rust code path.

rules.quote: NEVER use `#[link_name = "@Name@N"]` with `extern "fastcall"`!
rules.rule: Never combine `#[link_name = "@Name@N"]` with `extern "fastcall"`, because fastcall already adds its own decoration and the result is double-decorated.

rules.quote: Instead, use the actual function name directly in the `extern "fastcall"` block.
rules.rule: When declaring a fastcall function in Rust, use the actual function name directly in the `extern "fastcall"` block instead of a `#[link_name]` attribute.

rules.quote: Rust export must use `extern "C"`, NOT `extern "system"`
rules.rule: Export MiDumpPoolConsumers from Rust with `extern "C"`, not `extern "system"`, because the C declaration has no NTAPI and so uses cdecl.

rules.quote: Always add UART traces before suspected bugcheck paths
rules.rule: When investigating a suspected bugcheck path on ARM64, add UART traces before that path runs.

rules.quote: Use direct PL011 MMIO writes (0x09000000) for critical traces
rules.rule: For critical ARM64 traces, use direct PL011 MMIO writes to 0x09000000 so the output bypasses DbgPrint and BRK and is always visible.

rules.quote: GT_TRACE must remain always-on for ARM64 QEMU builds
rules.rule: Keep GT_TRACE always enabled in ARM64 QEMU builds.

rules.quote: Any code that allocates kernel VAs dynamically must ensure PDE hierarchy exists
rules.rule: When code allocates kernel virtual addresses dynamically on ARM64, ensure the PDE hierarchy exists for those addresses.

rules.quote: Device memory MMIO writes (not standard barriers) are needed to synchronize QEMU's TCG JIT cache
rules.rule: To synchronize QEMU's TCG JIT cache, use device-memory MMIO writes rather than standard barriers.

rules.quote: NEVER use `ddk::*` (conflicts with base::*)
rules.rule: Never use a `ddk::*` glob import when translating C to Rust, because it conflicts with `base::*`.

rules.quote: Selective imports only.
rules.rule: Import only specific items from `ddk` instead of using glob imports.

rules.quote: `extern "system"` for callbacks
rules.rule: Declare callback functions with `extern "system"` when translating C to Rust.

rules.quote: Cast `PsGetCurrentProcess()` to `*mut _EPROCESS` for field access
rules.rule: Cast the result of `PsGetCurrentProcess()` to `*mut _EPROCESS` before accessing its fields.

rules.quote: Wrap in `Some()` for Option<unsafe extern fn> fields
rules.rule: Wrap function pointer values in `Some()` when assigning to `Option<unsafe extern fn>` fields.

rules.quote: `core::ptr::addr_of_mut!()` for struct field pointers
rules.rule: Use `core::ptr::addr_of_mut!()` to create raw pointers to struct fields.

rules.quote: LONG_PTR fields: InterlockedIncrementSizeT/DecrementSizeT
rules.rule: For LONG_PTR fields, use `InterlockedIncrementSizeT` and `InterlockedDecrementSizeT` for atomic increment and decrement.

rules.quote: Post-Processor (postprocess.py) — SAFE transforms only
rules.rule: Restrict the post-processor (postprocess.py) to safe transforms only.

rules.quote: **NOT** union field access
rules.rule: Do not perform union field access transforms in the post-processor.

rules.quote: Be skeptical**: "smoke tests pass" only meant the weakened markers were hit, NOT that the desktop was reached.
rules.rule: Be skeptical of reports that smoke tests pass: a pass only means the weakened markers were hit, not that the desktop was reached.

rules.quote: listen before QEMU
rules.rule: When using the Unix socket serial client, listen on the socket before starting QEMU (server-socket pattern).

rules.quote: i386: `if=none` without device to avoid FreeLDR crash on unpartitioned disk
rules.rule: For the i386 scratch qcow2 disk used for savevm/loadvm, configure it with `if=none` and no device to avoid the FreeLDR crash on an unpartitioned disk.
